source.title: On the loss landscape of a class of deep neural networks with no bad local valleys
source.authors: Quynh Nguyen; Mahesh Chandra Mukkamala; Matthias Hein

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent garbling or truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a loss-landscape result for a specially constructed class of networks and reports training-error experiments on CIFAR-10, bearing on V1 and V3 but not reproducing their original recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper's main theoretical results are not empirical training outcomes. Experimental results with training error appear in Table 2 and Appendix F: record separate CIFAR-10 results for the original and output-skip networks, sigmoid and softplus activations, and the randomized-feature and full-SGD procedures. CIFAR-10 150-layer softplus results in Figure 5 are described in text but have no numeric values. Test accuracy results do not bear on the claim and are omitted.
record.test_reason: Table 2 directly tests V1 through CIFAR-10 training accuracy under full-network SGD, using sigmoid and softplus networks with and without output-layer connections. It does not test V3's depth degradation comparison or identity residual shortcuts. The landscape theorem does not establish convergence of SGD.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors prove favorable loss-landscape properties for a specified class of overparameterized networks with output connections, and empirically find zero training error with better generalization from full-network SGD than from fixed random features. The theorem does not guarantee SGD convergence, permits non-strict local minima, and does not directly cover the max-pooling VGG experiments in Table 2.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes networks with at least N hidden units connected directly to output units and tests them with SGD+Nesterov on MNIST/CIFAR-10; it does not use the cited papers' recipes for the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcomes varied with activation and architecture: sigmoid VGG models without output-layer skips reached 10 training accuracy, whereas their skip variants reached 100; sigmoid DenseNet reached 100 without the added output skips. On the 150-layer softplus setting, output skips converged to zero training error within 200 epochs while the plain network failed after 1000 epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Output-only SGD on fixed random features achieves 100% CIFAR-10 training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently many fixed random hidden features with learned linear output weights can interpolate the training labels.

fits_no_version.finding: A 150-layer, width-10 fully connected softplus network with output connections reaches zero training error within 200 epochs; its plain counterpart fluctuates and fails to converge after 1000 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Direct hidden-to-output connections can improve optimization of very deep fully connected softplus networks on a CIFAR-10 subset.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated analytic-activation and architecture assumptions, the loss landscape has no bad local valleys or suboptimal strict local minima; non-strict local minima remain possible.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks with sufficiently many independently weighted hidden-to-output connections have favorable loss-landscape topology under the theorem's assumptions.

record.problems: The experiments use specialized output-layer skip connections and do not test standard CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 recipes in the versions. The CIFAR-10 training-accuracy table gives no uncertainty; the 150-layer comparison is described in text but exact values are figure-only. The paper does not report CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random-label experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Training-accuracy rows for the CIFAR-10 random-feature procedure are retained (R17–R24). Test accuracy rows are omitted because test accuracy does not measure training classification error. Table 1 MNIST results are outside the listed CIFAR benchmark settings. Other test-accuracy results in Tables 2, 4, and 5 do not bear on the claim. Figure 3 loss-landscape visualization does not report training classification error.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; controlled model-size, early-stopping, and regularization comparisons; Adam. The reported results concern clean CIFAR-10 with sigmoid or softplus and the study's training schedules.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, standard-initialization failure-frequency measurement, or extra-neuron sweep.
No controlled depth degradation experiment in plain batch-normalized CNNs, matched identity residual shortcuts, special initialization of deep plain tanh networks, or Fixup.
No initialization comparison or measurement relating signal and gradient propagation to learning speed or trainable depth.
No initial stability threshold, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, or edge-of-stability experiment.
No matched normalization comparison, higher-learning-rate tolerance test, or Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Output-layer connections should not be treated as identity residual shortcuts. Table 2 training accuracies are percentages; uncertainty shown for test accuracy should not be assigned to training accuracy. Appendix F qualifies the nominal 300-epoch schedule with 1000 epochs for sigmoid skip-SGD and 5000 for sigmoid skip-rand.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-100, corrupted-label, or random-label experiment; no comparison of smaller model sizes or early stopping. CIFAR-10 experiments use special output skip-connections and the stated training schedule.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or neuron-count sweep.

Does not compare identity shortcuts or batch-normalized networks; tested output-layer skip-connections, not identity residual shortcuts. The deep plain-network comparison is for 150-layer softplus on a small CIFAR-10 subset.
No comparison of initialization schemes or signal/gradient propagation.
No learning-rate stability threshold or curvature measurement.
